applicability.jurisdiction_or_standard_context: UK/Eurocode-oriented portal-frame and member-design guidance. Use as concept and modeling guidance only.

claims.text: Steel member stability checks depend on whether the member is sufficiently restrained and on the relevant unbraced or buckling length.
Portal-frame rafters and columns require out-of-plane restraint assumptions to be tracked separately from the in-plane frame analysis.
Purlins, side rails, stays, and bracing can provide useful restraint only when their connectivity, stiffness, and load path are represented explicitly enough for the intended check.

limitations: The card does not decide whether a restraint is adequate for a code check.
Secondary members must not be assumed to restrain primary members unless the modeled system and check context justify it.

pages_used: Member design: Uniform members in bending
Portal frames: Out-of-plane stability and Plan bracing

summary: Member stability reasoning should preserve what restrains a member, which direction it restrains, and the unbraced length implied by those restraints.
title: Member Restraint And Unbraced Length
